answer: Agents can bind each account to a proof-of-personhood credential issued after an in-person check, while keeping the credential private and revealing only a unique nullifier for each market or epoch. The contract accepts one vote or claim per nullifier, so making many accounts does not multiply influence. An attacker must recruit and verify real people, paying for coordination and risking exposure; fake keys alone cannot create the signal. A coordinated ripple of genuine participants is costly to sustain, even at the nadir of credential renewal.
